methodological_rigor.justification: This retrospective imaging study evaluates SAM variants for breast nodule segmentation on DCE-MRI, with 103 cases collected (80 malignant, 23 benign) and radiologist-drawn contours as ground truth; four benign cases with very small nodules were excluded, leaving 99 cases for analysis. The experimental comparisons are reasonably structured (SAM vs MedSAM initialization; adaptive vs fixed prompt boxes; breast organ mask variants) and use 5-fold cross-validation with consistent preprocessing and training settings. However, no external validation set is used, class imbalance is acknowledged, and the statistical testing description is internally inconsistent (stating metrics are non-normal yet describing paired t-tests before Nemenyi post-hoc comparisons), which weakens confidence in inferential claims.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is clinically adjacent (breast MRI lesion segmentation could support detection/assessment workflows), but the endpoints are algorithmic (Dice and HD95) rather than patient outcomes. The dataset is single-center retrospective and focused on single-nodule cases, with acknowledged limitations including small sample size and lack of multiple-nodule cases. Under the Oxford hierarchy (which centers on clinical evidence for interventions), this technical model-development evaluation best maps to level 5.

reporting_quality.justification: No single canonical reporting standard in the provided list clearly fits segmentation benchmarking, so "other" is the closest option; the manuscript does report key dataset properties, preprocessing, model variants, training hyperparameters, and cross-validation design. Results are summarized across models with Dice/HD95 and qualitative figure descriptions, and limitations (small single-center dataset; imbalance; multiple-nodule absence) are explicitly noted. Data and code sharing are not described in the blinded text (no repository, model weights, or code access information), limiting reproducibility beyond the narrative.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is a pragmatic configuration study applying SAM/MedSAM to breast DCE-MRI and systematically comparing initialization, prompt box strategy, and breast masking under a constrained data regime. The work does not introduce a new segmentation architecture, and the paper itself notes that hybrid SAM variants in the literature report higher Dice, positioning this as incremental optimization rather than a first-in-class method. Its contribution is mainly empirical guidance for deployment-oriented choices (e.g., MedSAM initialization and fixed prompt boxes) within this modality.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable and organized around the three configuration axes (initial weights, organ mask, prompt box) with clear descriptions of preprocessing and training settings. Methods include concrete numeric details (image sizes, normalization, optimizer settings, cross-validation folds) and the discussion connects results to practical feasibility (adaptive boxes being impractical). Presentation would improve with more direct in-text reporting of the key numerical results (tables are referenced) and with a clearer, statistically coherent description of hypothesis testing choices.

key_strengths: Clear, deployment-oriented comparison of SAM configuration choices (MedSAM initialization; fixed vs adaptive prompt boxes; breast mask variants) on breast DCE-MRI.
Reasonable experimental hygiene with consistent preprocessing, stated training hyperparameters, and 5-fold cross-validation on 99 analyzed cases.
Candid limitations section (small single-center dataset, benign/malignant imbalance, exclusion of very small lesions, lack of multiple-nodule cases).
key_concerns: No external or multi-center validation; results may not generalize beyond the single cohort and the specific DCE-MRI setting.
Statistical analysis description is inconsistent (non-normal metrics but paired t-tests) and key numeric results are largely table-referenced rather than integrated into the main text.
Reproducibility is limited by lack of stated data/code/model availability in the blinded manuscript.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a useful but modest-scope configuration/benchmarking study; with stronger statistical reporting, clearer in-text quantitative results, and ideally external validation, it could fit a mid-tier venue focused on medical imaging methods.
